subject.title: [Bug]: Google Chat: Space/Group messages silently ignored (DMs work correctly)

question: Should Google Chat Space `MESSAGE` events that reach the HTTP endpoint count as activation when annotation-based mention detection fails, or should OpenClaw keep strict `USER_MENTION`/`botUser` matching and improve diagnostics only?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the permanent behavior changes a group trigger-authorization boundary and depends on the exact Google Chat event contract observed in live Space payloads.

options.title: Live-Prove Then Relax Activation
options.body: Collect a redacted v2026.6.11 Space event payload and, if Google only delivers mentioned HTTP-endpoint Space messages for this surface, treat the delivered event as activation while retaining sender and group allowlists.

options.title: Keep Strict Mention Matching
options.body: Require `USER_MENTION` annotations to match `botUser`, and add clearer setup validation/logging for cases where Google sends an unexpected annotation shape.

options.title: Consolidate Into Broader Space Work
options.body: Move the remaining behavior under a broader Google Chat Space/thread routing plan, accepting that this user-visible bug remains open until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Live-Prove Then Relax Activation
recommendation.body: Collect a redacted v2026.6.11 Space event payload and, if Google only delivers mentioned HTTP-endpoint Space messages for this surface, treat the delivered event as activation while retaining sender and group allowlists.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has recent history in the Google Chat monitor/access-policy area and the group-trigger safety boundary this decision would change.
